title: The Next Trillion Internet Users Still Don’t Have an Identity — Adi Singh, AgentMail
talk_summary: A philosophical talk about agent identity arguing that agents should adopt existing human surfaces (email, Slack, DNS trust layers) rather than new identity specs, illustrated by AgentMail's email-inbox API and an agent signup flow built with a phone carrier. It contains almost no engineering technique for orchestration, cost, or review quality; the only concrete mechanism is giving agents a real email inbox as a durable contact/audit point.

takeaways.technique: Give each agent a real email inbox as its durable identity/contact point
takeaways.what_they_do: In the Telnyx agent-signup flow, the skill.md calls an API to provision an email address so the agent can receive verification codes, get an API key, and remain reachable for balance alerts, suspensions, and support.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they added was an API call to our endpoint where we could provide the agent the email address if need be so it doesn't hallucinate

takeaways.technique: Treat the agent's surface as both trust and attack surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that email's trust (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, audit trails) comes with phishing and prompt-injection risk, and that giving agents a human's own inbox/WhatsApp expands blast radius.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the node is the trust surface right now and it drives adoption. But it can also be very well the attack surface
